tx_girls_of_juarez.blurb: A small cluster of boulder problems in the Upper Lost Boulders section of North Mountain at Hueco Tanks, east of El Paso. There are a dozen or so lines, spread from easy V1 up through the middle grades, with the bulk of them in the V4 to V5 range and a single standout at V10. The spot stays cold and shady and loses light early, so it suits a morning start or a cooler day more than a warm afternoon. Landings can be uneven, so bring pads and spotters. It works well for climbers who want a few classic mid-grade problems in one place, plus one serious project for the strong.

tx_house_of_pain.blurb: A steep limestone sport wall at Reimers Ranch in the hills west of Austin, tucked down the canyon from the Insect Wall and easy to spot because it is the face not draped in vines. Thirteen routes, almost all bolted, with the heart of the wall in the 5.12 range, a few at 5.11, and a small handful pushing into 5.13 and one at 5.14. The rock is pocketed limestone and the cliff sits in shade for much of the day, which makes it a sensible choice in warmer weather. Expect hard, sustained face and roof climbing rather than anything for beginners.
